images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of SALA.Left:unpaired human and robot videos are related only through language descriptions of their atomic actions.Middle:supervising a latent action tokenizer with these relations organizes latent actions by action semantics rather than by scene.Right:through the aligned latent actions, human videos supervise the same policy that controls the robot: more human-video pre-training lowers the validation error of robot action prediction without additional robot data, and more task-specific human video in post-training raises the real-world success rate.

Figure 2:Method overview.(a) Latent action tokenizer.Robot (blue) and human (orange) clips share the visual encoderℰθ\mathcal{E}_{\theta}, the SoftVQ quantizer𝒬ϕ\mathcal{Q}_{\phi}, and the visual decoder𝒢v\mathcal{G}_{v}; only robot clips train the action decoder𝒢a\mathcal{G}_{a}. Language similaritiesSℓS^{\ell}between atomic-action descriptions define soft neighborhoodsPP, which supervise the latent neighborhoodsQQderived from latent similaritiesSzS^{z}, with gradients stopped through robot latents.(b) VLA policy.The frozen tokenizer labels each clip with latent action tokens𝐲\mathbf{y}, each a categorical distribution over the codebook. Latent queries in the action expert predict𝐲^\hat{\mathbf{y}}through a latent head, supervised byℒLA\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{LA}}for both human and robot data; robot data additionally train flow matching withℒFMR\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{FM}}^{R}. In the action expert, blue inputs (state and noisy actions) are used only for robot data, whereas green latent queries are used for both human and robot data.

Figure 3:Real-world data.Left: examples of the large-scale data used in pre- and mid-training,i.e., egocentric human videos𝒟H{\color[rgb]{0.9,0.45,0.05}\mathcal{D}_{H}}and robot teleoperation data𝒟R{\color[rgb]{0.1523,0.2109,0.7617}\mathcal{D}_{R}}. Right: the four downstream tasks, each performed by a person, recorded as human demonstrations𝒟Htask{\color[rgb]{0.9,0.45,0.05}\mathcal{D}_{H}^{\mathrm{task}}}, and by the robot under teleoperation, recorded as teleoperated demonstrations𝒟Rtask{\color[rgb]{0.1523,0.2109,0.7617}\mathcal{D}_{R}^{\mathrm{task}}}.

Figure 6:Cross-embodiment retrieval for human pre-training videos.Each human query (left) and its three nearest robot clips over all tasks, under the reconstruction-only tokenizer (middle) and SALA (right).

Figure 10:Clusters of latent actions.For three pairs of atomic actions infigure5(a), k-means (k=2k=2) is applied to the 80ARX-X5latents of each tokenizer, 20 per atomic action and scene type. Each half-row shows one cluster: its composition in the header and four of its clips. Without alignment (recon. only), the two clusters are the clean and the randomized clips, each mixing both atomic actions; with alignment, each cluster is one atomic action, covering both scene types. Filled circle: clean scene; open triangle: randomized scene.

Figure 14:Real-world platform.The Sharpa North robot comprises (a) a head-mounted stereo camera, (b) two 7-DoF arms, (c) two 22-DoF Sharpa Wave dexterous hands, (d) two wrist-mounted fisheye cameras, (e) a torso, and (f) a wheeled base.
